reason: The cited evidence shows that remelting strategies can control microstructure in SS316L (E1) and that single-pass laser cladding of AlCoCrFeNi HEA yields defect-free surfaces (E2), but neither passage directly supports the claims that remelting reduces thermal gradients, homogenizes HEA microstructure, or improves dimensional precision and mechanical properties. The key premises lack specific prior evidence.
premises: Laser remelting of a deposited layer reduces residual thermal gradients
Laser remelting promotes microstructural homogenization in HEAs
Reduced thermal gradients and homogenization decrease fabrication defects (porosity, cracks)
Defect reduction improves dimensional precision and mechanical integrity
In-situ remelting is effective under standard AM conditions for HEAs
